Thy father, did he not eat and drink? When he did judgment and justice, It was then well with him:<div eID="gen60481" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60482" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>He judged the cause of the poor and needy, It was then well <hi type="italic">with him; </hi>Was not this to know me? saith Jehovah:<div eID="gen60482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60483" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>For thy eye and thy heart are not Except on thy covetousness, And on shedding innocent blood, And on rapacity and oppression, to do <hi type="italic">them.</hi><div eID="gen60483" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60484" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>Therefore thus saith Jehovah, Of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah the king of Judea, They shall not bewail him, — “Ah, my brother! Ah, sister!” They shall not bewail him, — “Ah, Lord! Ah, his glory!”<div eID="gen60484" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60485" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>With the burial of an ass shall he be buried, Drawn out and cast forth Beyond the gates of Jerusalem.<div eID="gen60485" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60486" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>Ascend into Lebanon and cry, And on Bashan lift up thy voice, And cry all around, For destroyed are all thy lovers.<div eID="gen60486" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60487" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>I spake to thee in thy tranquillity, Thou saidst, “I will not hear:” It has been thy manner from thy youth That thou didst not hear my voice.<div eID="gen60487" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60488" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>Thy pastors shall the wind consume, And thy lovers, into exile shall they go: Surely ashamed shalt thou then be, And blush for all thy wickedness.<div eID="gen60488" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60489" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Thou hast set thy seat on Lebanon, Thou hast made thy nest among the cedars: How gracious wilt thou be When come on thee shall sorrows, The pain as of one in travail!<div eID="gen60489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60490" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>Live do I, saith Jehovah; Were Coniah the son of Jehoiakim the king of Judah A sealing ring on my right hand, I would thence pluck thee off:<div eID="gen60490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60491" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>And I will deliver thee Into the hand of those who seek thy life, And into the hand of those whose face thou dreadest, Even into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar The king of Babylon, And into the hand of the Chaldeans:<div eID="gen60491" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60492" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>And I will cast thee and thy mother who bare thee Into a foreign land where ye were not born, And there shall ye die;<div eID="gen60492" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60493" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27 </hi>And into the land they set their mind to return, Thither they shall not return.<div eID="gen60493" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60494" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28 </hi>Is this man Coniah a despised <hi type="italic">and </hi>broken statue? Is he a vessel in which there is no delight? Why are they east forth, he and his seed, And thrown to a land which they have not known?<div eID="gen60494" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60495" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29 </hi>Land! land! land! hear the word of Jehovah, —<div eID="gen60495" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60496" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30 </hi>Thus saith Jehovah, Write ye this man childless, A man who shall not prosper in his days; Nay, none of his seed shall prosper, Sitting on the throne of David, And ruling any more in Judah.<div eID="gen60496" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen60465"/> <div sID="gen60497"/> <div sID="gen60498" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 23<div eID="gen60498" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60499" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Woe to the pastors who destroy and scatter The flock of my pastures! saith Jehovah;<div eID="gen60499" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60500" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Therefore thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Concerning the pastors who feed my people, — Ye have scattered my flock and driven them away, And ye have not visited them; Behold, I will visit upon you The wickedness of your doings, saith Jehovah:<div eID="gen60500" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60501" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>But I will gather the remnant of my sheep From all the lands to which I shall drive them, And cause them to return to their own folds, And they shall become fruitful and multiply;<div eID="gen60501" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60502" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>And I will raise up over them pastors Who shall feed them; And they shall no more fear nor dread, Nor shall they fail, saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen60502" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60503" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Behold, the days are coming, saith Jehovah, That I will raise up to David a righteous branch, And reign shall a king, And prudently shall he act; He will do judgment and justice in the land.<div eID="gen60503" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60504" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>In his days saved shall be Judah, And Israel shall dwell in confidence: And this is the name by which they shall call him, Jehovah Our Righteousness<div eID="gen60504" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60505" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Therefore, behold, the days will come, saith Jehovah, In which it shall no more be said, “Live does Jehovah,” Who brought the children of Israel from the land of Egypt;<div eID="gen60505" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60506" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>But rather, “Live does Jehovah,” who has brought up And led the seed of the house of Israel From the land of the north, and all the lands To which I had driven them; And they shall dwell in their own land.<div eID="gen60506" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60507" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>On account of the prophets, Broken is my heart within me, Disjointed are all my bones; I am become like a drunken man Who has been overcome by wine, On account of Jehovah, And on account of the words of his holiness;<div eID="gen60507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60508" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>For with adulterers the land is filled: For on account of perjury mourned has the land, Dried up have the pastures of the desert; And their course has been evil, And their strength not right.<div eID="gen60508" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60509" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>For both prophet and priest have acted wickedly; Even in my house have I found Their wickedness, saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen60509" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60510" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Therefore their way shall be to them slippery; In darkness shall they stumble and fall therein; For I shall bring on them evil, The year of their visitation, saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen60510" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60511" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>In the prophets of Samaria have I seen fatuity, They prophesied by Baal, And made my people Israel to go astray:<div eID="gen60511" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60512" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>But in the prophets of Jerusalem Have I seen depravity; By adultery and walking in falsehood They even strengthen the hands of the wicked, That they may not turn, each from his wickedness: They shall be all to me as Sodom, And its inhabitants as Gomorrah.<div eID="gen60512" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60513" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>Therefore thus saith Jehovah of hosts Concerning these prophets, — I will feed them with a deadly poison, And give them waters of gall to drink; For from the prophets of Jerusalem Has gone forth impiety through all the laud.<div eID="gen60513" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60514" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, — Hear ye not the words of the prophets Who prophesy to you; They make you to be vain; A vision of their own heart do they speak, <hi type="italic">And </hi>not from the mouth of Jehovah;<div eID="gen60514" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60515" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Who say to those who despise me, Spoken has Jehovah, “Peace shall be to you;” And to all who walk in the wickedness of their own hearts They say, “Come upon you shall not evil;<div eID="gen60515" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60516" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>For who hath been in the counsel of Jehovah, And seen and heard his word? Who hath listened to his word and heard it?”<div eID="gen60516" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60517" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Behold the whirlwind of Jehovah! With fury it goeth forth; Even the impending whirlwind; On the head of the ungodly shall it fall:<div eID="gen60517" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60518" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>Turn back shall not the anger of Jehovah Till he has done and confirmed The thoughts of his own heart: In the extremity of days Ye shall fully understand this.<div eID="gen60518" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60519" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>I sent not the prophets, yet they have run; I spoke not to them, yet they have prophesied.<div eID="gen60519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60520" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>But if they had stood in my counsel, Surely they would have made my people hear my words, And turned them from their evil way, And from the wickedness of their doings?<div eID="gen60520" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60521" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Am I a God at hand, saith Jehovah, And not a God afar off?<div eID="gen60521" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60522" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>Can a man hide himself in coverts That I could not see him? saith Jehovah; Do not I fill the heavens and the earth? saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen60522" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60523" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>I have heard what the prophets say Who prophesy falsely in my name, Saying, “I have dreamed, I have dreamed.”<div eID="gen60523" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60524" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>How long will it be in the heart of the prophets To prophesy falsehood, Yea, of the prophets of the deceit of their own heart!<div eID="gen60524" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60525" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27 </hi>Who think to make my people forget My name by their own dreams, Which they relate, each to his friend, As forgotten my name have their fathers through Baal.<div eID="gen60525" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60526" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28 </hi>The prophet who hath a dream, He will relate a dream; And he with whom is my word, He will speak my word of truth: What is the chaff to the wheat? saith Jehovah.<div eID="gen60526" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60527" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">29 </hi>Is not my word like fire? saith Jehovah, And like the hammer that breaks the stone?<div eID="gen60527" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60528" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30 </hi>Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets, saith Jehovah, Who steal my words, each from his friend:<div eID="gen60528" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen60529" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31 </hi>Behold, I am against the prophets, saith Jehovah, Who elevate their own tongue, And say, “<hi type="italic">It</hi> <

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="29" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. XXIX.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 NOW these <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the words of the letter, that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem unto the residue of the elders, which were car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried away captives, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">There were two carryings into the captivity of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> the latter about 11 or 12 years after the former, the first was in the time of <ns0:hi>Iehojachin,</ns0:hi> of which we read in 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 24.14. <ns0:hi>When the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand cap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tives, and all the craftsmen and smiths were carried away,</ns0:hi> as we read there, amongst whom were some Priests and Prophets.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 After that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kings 24.12. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Jeconiah the king, and the queen, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Chamber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lains.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> the eunuchs, the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the carpenters, and the smiths were departed from Jerusalem <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">After this Captivity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 By the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, whom Zede<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kiah king of Judah sent unto Babylon to Nebu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chadnezzar king of Babylon, saying <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> the King of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> having some occasion to send two messengers, named <ns0:hi>Elasa</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gemariah</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> whether to carry his tribute money, or upon what other errand is not expressed. <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> knowing that as there were some false Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> who fed people with hopes of a speedy re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turn, so there were some with them in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> who did the like, (two of which he afterwards in this Chapter reflecteth up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on) writeth the following letter, and sends it by these two mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sengers, to quiet the peoples minds, and to help to compose their spirits, disturb'd by these false Prophets, and raised up to vain and idle hopes for which there was no ground at all.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 Thus saith the LORD of hosts the God of Israel, unto all that are carried away captives, whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem to Babylon <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">So as this Letter was not wrote from himself advising them charitably, but he had commission from God, by whom he mindeth them, as the principal efficient cause they were order<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to be carried away, though their own sins were the merito<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rious cause<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi> with his Captains and Souldiers were the instrumental cause.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">ver. 28.</ns0:note> Build ye houses, and dwell <ns0:hi>in them,</ns0:hi> and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Take ye wives, and beget sons and daugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters, and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, that they may bear sons and daughters, that ye may be increased there, and not diminished <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">That is, be not uneasie in your minds, not resolving what to do, through the prophesies of the false Prophets, that tell you the Captivity shall be but two years, or at least very short<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> But do all things which you would do, if <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> were to be your fixed habitation, (as it is like to be for seventy years, say the Prophets, what they please) Marry, and give, and take in Marriage, do whatsoever it becometh prudent men to do, who would accommodate themselves in a place, where they are like to abide, and preserve their Families, that they might not be utterly extinguished. The words must not be understood as a precept, obliging all in the Captivity to do every of these things, which it may be they were not all able to do, but as a counsel and advice not to forbear any thing of this nature, which they would do, if they did fully believe they were to abide in a place seventy years.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And seek the peace of the city, whither I have caused you to be carried away captives <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That is, seek to God for it, or rather, live peaceably in it, and by all lawful means seek the welfare of it, do not raise any tumults or seditions, nor take part with those that do.</ns0:note>, and pray unto the LORD for it <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And while your Captivity lasts do you pray for it, (from whence those who think that Christ hath added new moral precepts, and reckon this precept of praying for enemies as one, may under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand, that praying for enemies was but a branch of that love to our Neighbour, which God required under the Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment) for it was lawful for them to pray against <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> at other times, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 137.8. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 51.35. but when God hath put a yoke upon our necks, we must patiently wait until he takes it off. The Lawyers say that <ns0:hi>Protection requireth Allegiance to Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vernours</ns0:hi>; This Text lets us know also that it requireth our prayers for them; though they be Conquerours and Tyrants.</ns0:note>, for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">For God having by his providence cast us under their power, our peace dependeth upon theirs.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 ¶ For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Let not your prophets, and your diviners that <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> in the midst of you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 14.14. and 23.21. and 27.15.</ns0:note> deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Lord knows that you have a company of false Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, that tell you other things, and promise you a sudden re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turn out of your Captivity, pretending to know it by Revela<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion from God, or by divination, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> or to have it discovered to them in dreams. It is the will of God that you should not hearken to them, for they do but deceive you, and ye are ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessary to your own ruine, they see you are pleased to hear such stories, and that causeth them to dream, as <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 5.31. <ns0:hi>The prophets prophesie falsly, and the priests bear rule by their means, and my people love to have it so,</ns0:hi> thus <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 30.10. <ns0:hi>They said to the seers, see not, and to the prophets, prophesie not to us right things, speak un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to us smooth things, prophesie deceits.</ns0:hi> False teachers and guides of peoples souls are the greatest plague can befal a Nation, people from them expecting to hear the mind of God, and for the most part, people are accessary to their own ruine, in them it can indeed hardly be imagined, what other temptation, per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons whose office it is to reveal the mind of God, should have to do otherwise, but the humouring and pleasing of a corrupt people, who through their fondness of their lusts are not pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tient of sound Doctrine, so as though the Church of God hath in all Ages been troubled with dreamers, yet it is a wicked people that causeth them to dream.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 For they prophesie <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>in a li<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> falsly unto you in my name; I have not sent them, saith the LORD.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:39" />10 ¶ For thus saith the LORD, that after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon, I will visit you, and perform my good word to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards you, in causing you to return to this place <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">From this Text appears that the seventy years Captivity were to be accounted from the first carrying into Captivity in the time of <ns0:hi>Iehojachin,</ns0:hi> so that eleven years of it were elapsed, before <ns0:hi>Z<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>kiah</ns0:hi> was carried away. Whatever, saith the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet, these dreamers tell you, you must abide 70 years in <ns0:hi>Baby<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lon</ns0:hi> accounted from your first going thither, it is therefore your Wisdom to acquiesce in the Will of God, and to compose your selves, and to incourage you, the Lord by me assureth you that after those seventy years shall be expired, a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> he hath now visit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed you with evil, so he will visit you for good, and fulfil the promise he hath made to you, and you shall return again to <ns0:hi>Ier<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>salem</ns0:hi>: we have the fulfilling of this recorded in 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.21.22. <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 1.1. The promise was before, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 25.12. and 27.22. <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> understood it from the words of this Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.2. which put him upon prayer, at the ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />piration of that time.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 For I know the thoughts that I think to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>end and expectation.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> expected end <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This deliverance will not depend upon your Merits, but upon my own Mercy<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and kind thoughts and purposes I have for the seed of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> my servant and I am resolved in my own thoughts what to do. I intend not the blotting out of the name of <ns0:hi>Isr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> from the Earth<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but to give such an end to their trou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble as themselves expect and desire, though not so soon as they may expect it, being deceived by their Prophets. There shall be an end of your Captivity in my time, and that is after you shall have fulfilled seventy years in that Captivity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Then shall ye <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Dan. 9.3. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">I will not onely give you a tempora<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Salvation and delive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rance, and bring you into your own land, but you shall go thi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther with new hearts, you shall worship Idols no more, but you shall worship me, and be serious and diligent in your addresses and applications to me, and I will listen to you in those appli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cations.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lev. 26.40. Deut. 30.1.</ns0:note> ye shall seek me, and find <ns0:hi>me,</ns0:hi> when ye shall search for me with all your heart <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">That is, sincerely; as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 119.2.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 4.7. Psal. 32.6. & 46.2. Isa. 55.6.</ns0:note> I will be found of you, saith the LORD, and I will turn away your captivity, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 23.3.</ns0:note> I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places, whither I have driven you, saith the LORD, and I will bring you a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gain into the place, whence I caused you to be car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ried away captive <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This verse containeth no more than was said before, one<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly it is repeated in a little different phrase, for the further con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firmation of their Faith, and the promise is a little inlarged. God saith he will be <ns0:hi>found of them</ns0:hi>; that is, he will answer them. It is expressed in this notion to correspond with the term <ns0:hi>seek<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:hi> by which prayer is expressed, and to let us know, that those that will have Gods favour must <ns0:hi>find it</ns0:hi>; which implyeth a seeking, and inquiry after it. The promise which before men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned onely their return from <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> is inlarged, and made here to extend to all places whither they were driven, for though the body of the people were carried to <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> yet it is more than probable, that many of them shifted for themselves into other Countries, and were in Exile, but not in Captivity. <ns0:hi>Cyrus</ns0:hi> his Proclamation, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.22, 23. extended to his whole Empire.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 ¶ Because ye have said, The LORD hath raised us up prophets in Babylon <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The Prophet here turneth his speech to some wicked <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that were in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> or in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> and more believed some false Prophets, who told them of a much quicker return, th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n <ns0:hi>Ieremy</ns0:hi> telling them the truth from the mouth of God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 <ns0:hi>Know,</ns0:hi> that thus saith the LORD, of the king that sitteth upon the throne of David <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The word <ns0:hi>know</ns0:hi> is, as some think, needlesly supplied, for the following Particle might be as well translated, <ns0:hi>for,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>because,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>therefo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>e.</ns0:hi> By the King he meaneth <ns0:hi>Zedekiah,</ns0:hi> whom he chuseth to express under the notion of him that sitteth upon the throne of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> to take away the vain hopes which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> conceived from the promises which God had made to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and to his seed.</ns0:note>, and of all the people that dwell in this city, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> of your brethren that are not gone forth with you into captivity.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Behold I will send upon them the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 24.10.</ns0:note> sword, the famine and the pestilence, and will make them like <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 24.8:</ns0:note> vile figs that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And I will persecute them with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 28.25. chap. 15.4. & 34.17.</ns0:note> will deliver them to be removed to all the kingdoms of the earth, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>for a curse.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 42.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> to be a curse, and an astonishment, and an hissing, and a re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proach among all the Nations whither I have driven them <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">These verses contain no more then the threatning which we have had more then once before, he had compared them to vile Figs, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 24.8. and <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 9. and 10. there threatned them with being made a <ns0:hi>reproach,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>proverb,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>taunt,</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>curse</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>consuming</ns0:hi> them with the <ns0:hi>sword, famine,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pestilence,</ns0:hi> the same thing before delivered by word of mouth to those in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> is here repeated in a letter to that part of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> to take them off from giving credit to their false Prophets whither in <ns0:hi>Iudaea</ns0:hi> or in <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> who deluded them with the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mises of a speedy return. Believe it (saith the Prophet) you shall be so far from returning whatever your idle Prophets tell you, that your Brethren that are here shall be brought to you or de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stroyed with the <ns0:hi>sword,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>amine,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Pestilence,</ns0:hi> or scattered into other Kingdoms, where they shall be made, a curse and an astonishment, and an hissing and a reproach.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Because they have not hearkned to my words, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">A contempt of the word of the Lord was the cause of this peoples ruine, and will be the cause of ruine to any people. See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 7.25. and 11.7, 8. and 17.23.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 25.4<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> & 32.33.</ns0:note> I sent unto them by my servants the prophets, rising up ear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, and sending <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Lest they should say that they onely disobeyed the Prophets<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> God mindeth them, that in not hearkning to them, they did not hearken to him. The same thing Christ saith of the Gospel Ministers, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 10.16. The not believing, or not obeying, what Ministers teach not in a due discharge of their office revealing the Will of God, is no contempt of God, but of them who for that cause deserve to be contemned, but supposing that what Ministers deliver be the Mind and Will of God revealed in holy Writ and but a true explication, and application of that, not to hearken to God, and not to hearken to them is the same thing.</ns0:note>, but ye would not hear saith the LORD <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Ye wilfully refused to believe them, speaking the Truth to you in my name, and to obey those monitions they gave you by my direction. All this was a not hearing God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 ¶ Hear ye therefore the word of the LORD, all ye of the captivity whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Those phrases <ns0:hi>I have sent,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>I have driven, &c.</ns0:hi> are dili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gently to be observed by us. There is no evil in Cities or Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions which is an evil of punishment, but whoever be the instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments to bring it, God is the Author of it. These phrases also signified to those <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> that God was likeliest to know best how long they should stay there because he sent them thither.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesie a lye unto you in my name, Behold I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he shall slay them before your eyes <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Of these two persons we read no more in Holy Writ; that they pretended to be Prophets, that they abused the name of God, pretending to reveal his Will, when as what they said was not the Will of God, but a falshood, we learn out of this verse, and that they were both of them burnt by the King of Babylon we find in <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 22. what the falshoods they published were, is not expressed, but it is most probable they were some of those that pretended that God had revealed to them, that within two years, or a short time, the Captives carried away with <ns0:hi>Iehoiakim</ns0:hi> should return out of <ns0:hi>Babylon.</ns0:hi> God here tells those that were of the Captivity, that those two Wretches should themselves be carried unto the Captivity of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> and there slain.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">See Gen. 4<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>20.</ns0:note> And of them shall be taken up a curse by all the captivity of Judah, which <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> in Baby<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lon, saying, The LORD make thee like Zedekiah, and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon rosted in the fire <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">As false Teachers are of the highest sort of Transgressors, speaking lies in the name and under pretence of the Authority of the God of Truth: So God in his providence ordinarily makes them the greatest examples of his vengeance. God threatneth to bring them to an end that should turn into a pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verb, that when men had a mind to curse others, wishing them the greatest evils, they should pray to God to make them like <ns0:hi>Ahab</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zedekiah,</ns0:hi> whom the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> burnt, or roasted in the fire, the word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifieth both, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 2.14. and roasting signifieth only to burn by degrees, which probably was the specifical punishment of these two false Prophets, for we learn from the instance of the three children, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 3.19. That the consuming of persons slowly in a fiery Furnace, was a kind of punishment in use amongst the <ns0:hi>Chaldaeans.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:39" />23 Because <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 23.14.</ns0:note> they have committed villany in Israel <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The reason here given must not be understood as the rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son of the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>'s punishment of them, but why God gave them up into his hands, because they had committed <ns0:hi>vil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lany</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>folly</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and have committed adultery with their neighbours wives <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Which is expounded <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y the next words, they had <ns0:hi>committed adultery with their neighbours wives.</ns0:hi> All sin is <ns0:hi>folly,</ns0:hi> and so called in Scripture, uncleanness particularly, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 34.7. here it is called <ns0:hi>villany,</ns0:hi> to denote the hainousness of it, especially in those whose office it was to teach others that they ought not to do it, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.22.
